newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seeks to cement closer ties with Asia.
newsitem.headline: EU seeks to cement closer ties with Asia.

text.p: The European Union, wary of the increasing political and economic muscle being flexed by its Asian partners, will discuss Monday ways of ensuring the relationship continues on an even keel.

EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels are due to finalise a common position for two key gatherings in Singapore next month -- one with their counterparts from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations or ASEAN and the other under the Europe-Asia Meeting, ASEM, umbrella.
"These are important rendezvous," said a diplomat from the Netherlands which, as current EU president under the 15-nation bloc's rotating system, is responsible for finalising a common EU position.
"Every year Asia is showing itself to be a more and more important region ... not just for Europe, but for the whole world."
The EU's ties with Asian organisations have gone through some rough patches in recent years -- particularly over relations between former colonial powers and their colonies.

Portugal, for example, has frequently protested through the EU about Indonesian policy in its former colony East Timor. The Netherlands, as Indonesia's former colonial power, also has an interest in this.
More recently, links betweem Asia and Europe have been strained by ASEAN plans to enlarge to take in Burma which the EU frequently criticises for human rights abuses.
ASEAN leaders consistently argue that such criticism would be like Asia complaining to the EU about its membership.

The ASEAN meeting on Feb. 13-14 will include new member Vietnam for the first time but, with plans to take in Cambodia, Laos and Burma in the near future, the EU is making sure it does not take the bloc lightly.
The EU has become ASEAN's third biggest trade partner with more than 70 billion European currency units ($85 billion) in goods and services changing hands in 1994-95.

The Feb. 15 ASEM meeting -- which takes in ASEAN members Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Philippines, Brunei and Vietnam with China, Japan and South Korea -- is to focus on establishing an Asia-Europe Foundation to fund cultural exchanges.
